findingsAndLessons.LESSON: A control that shells out to a tool the author happens to have installed is not a control: the source-prefix falsifier used `rg`, passed on this machine and died on the CI runner with `spawnSync rg ENOENT` (hauska-factory run 35390095381, 1 of 2004 tests). Rewritten as a pure-node tree scan and then proven non-vacuous in BOTH directions by mutation (a literal prefix typed into a code line in src/jobs/parcel-r5-zoning.mjs; a second producer of CORPUS_SOURCE_PREFIX exported from that file -- each made the test fail, naming the file and line). Lesson: prefer node, and if a scan must shell out, the test is only as portable as the tool.

CI is the only clone that matters: this defect was invisible locally and in the lane's own suite run, because local runs and CI runs differ in the tools on PATH. Running the suite locally is not evidence about CI.

findingsAndLessons.DEAD-END: Do NOT plan on running the job's own dry run without the cortex heavy-scan lease: every invocation takes one via grantHeavyScanLease, and a lane that retries on LEASE_HELD in a tight loop writes a durable refusal row per attempt (the first waiter here did, and it was killed for it). Read the live lease table, sleep to the holder's expiry, then attempt once.
findingsAndLessons.OPEN: The re-stamp path moves `updated_at` (it is in the UPDATE's SET clause). That is intended -- the citation really did change -- but a reader watching updated_at will see 387,231 rows move on the apply, and the seat's blast-radius expectations should say so before it runs.

The release re-resolves with the cell's OWN recorded (jurisdictionKey, districtCode), never the live zoningDistrict cell: a parcel whose zoning changed since its setback cells were written keeps the old code until the zoning rail's own change lands. Deliberate (it is the input the stale-match instrument measured with, which is why the dry run reproduces the prediction), and named in the job header's bypass list.
